Axolotl 0.2.0 adds type parameters, annotations, class literals, the type argument `*` and interface methods, so JUnit tests, Jackson
records and Spring entry points can be written in Axolotl, and comes with installers, which bring
their own Java runtime, and with `axl setup`, so the Gradle and Maven plugins no longer have to be
built from source.

## Downloads

The installers bring their own Java runtime, put `axl` on the `PATH` and run `axl setup`, which
copies the Axolotl libraries and the Gradle and Maven plugins into the local Maven repository:

- `axolotl-0.2.0-windows-x64-setup.exe`: Windows. Not signed, so SmartScreen asks first: *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
- `axolotl-0.2.0-macos-arm64.pkg`: macOS on Apple silicon. Not signed: see the [installation guide](https://github.com/succubus-uwu/axolotl/blob/v0.2.0/docs/install.md) for how to open it.
- `axolotl-0.2.0-linux-amd64.deb`: Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 or newer: `sudo apt install ./axolotl-0.2.0-linux-amd64.deb`.
- `axolotl-0.2.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`: other Linux systems. Unpack it and run `install.sh`, which needs no root.

Guides to installing and using the `axl` command line, in English and Russian:
`axolotl-0.2.0-windows-en.pdf`, `axolotl-0.2.0-macos-en.pdf`, `axolotl-0.2.0-linux-en.pdf` and the
`-ru` versions.

Without an installer:

- `axl-0.2.0.zip`: the command line compiler for Java 21. Unzip it, put `bin` on your `PATH` and run
  `axl setup` for the Gradle and Maven plugins.
- `axolotl-0.2.0.vsix`: the VS Code extension: `code --install-extension axolotl-0.2.0.vsix`.
- `axl-intellij-0.2.0.zip`: the IntelliJ IDEA plugin: *Settings | Plugins | Install Plugin from Disk*.

The Gradle and Maven plugins are not published to a public repository yet: `axl setup` installs them
into the local Maven repository, and projects find them there with `mavenLocal()`.

## What is new

Language:

- Type parameters: `data class Pair<A, B>(...)`, `interface Repository<K, V>`, `class Stack<T : Object>`
  and `fn largest<T : Comparable<T>>(xs: List<T>) -> T?`, so generic code no longer stays in Java.
- Annotations (`@Test`, `@JsonProperty("x")`), class literals `String.class` and the type argument `*`,
  so JUnit tests, Jackson records and Spring entry points can be written in Axolotl.
- Classes: interfaces that require methods, custom exceptions and other Java subclasses
  (`class NotFound(val id: String) : RuntimeException(...)`), `private` class parameters, constructors that
  delegate (`constructor(name: String) = this(name, "")`), and a private or annotated primary constructor
  (`class Parser private constructor(...)`). Sealed interfaces may have their implementations in other files of
  the package, which keep their Java names.
- Control flow: counting loops `for (i in 0 until n)`, `1..n`, `n downTo 0` with `step`, `break` and `continue`,
  `when` branches that are statements, and `attempt` exits (`attempt f() else e -> continue`).
- Errors: typed handlers `attempt X else e: IOException -> ...` catch one class, `use (val r = open()) { ... }`
  closes resources, and `attempt X else e -> throw Y` calls a Java method with a checked exception where no
  `Result` is wanted.
- Null safety at the boundary: public functions and constructors check non-null parameters on entry, so a `null`
  from Java fails at once and names the parameter (`--no-param-checks` turns this off). `==` on strings and data
  classes is an error, and numbers taken from a collection compare by value.

Tools:

- The installers and `axl setup`, so the Gradle and Maven plugins no longer have to be built from source.
- A compiler daemon: after the first command, `axl check`, `build` and `run` compile a small program in about a
  second instead of three to seven.
- `axl fmt`, also as formatting in the language server and *Reformat Code* in IntelliJ.
- Error Prone and NullAway check only the Java translated from `.axl` files, so hand-written Java in a mixed
  module keeps the warnings of plain javac (`--check-java` checks it too).
- Editors know every new construct; the language server reads library classes from the classpath.

Quality: the compiler went through seventeen rounds of review. The later rounds ported three real Java libraries
(Apache Commons CLI, java-diff-utils, Apache Commons CSV) to Axolotl and ran their own JUnit tests against the
ports, which found holes the language's own tests did not, such as null checks skipped next to a
`package-info.java`. After small test edits the ports pass 927 of 930, 165 of 165 and 973 of 974 tests.

Axolotl is now licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/succubus-uwu/axolotl/blob/v0.2.0/CHANGELOG.md) for details.

## Known limitations

- `var x = when` with lambdas in its branches needs a written type.
- Error Prone in Maven needs `.mvn/jvm.config`, and Gradle compiles in a forked JVM.
- The IntelliJ plugin reads only JDK classes for its checks, not the libraries on the classpath.
- An Axolotl library shows Java callers final classes, lists instead of arrays and no `throws`; the language guide
  shows the small Java interface that adapts such a class where Java callers need more.
- The compiler daemon is tested on Linux; on Windows it is used only from a console.
